title: DKIM signs X-Stoa-Injection-Source header which reader strips on receipt
description: In queue.rs drain_once: inject_source_header() is called first, then signer.sign(&article) signs the result. The X-Stoa-Injection-Source header is included in the DKIM canonical form. The reader strips that header before storing the article. Any downstream verifier (or the reader itself) checking DKIM on the stored/forwarded article will see a hash mismatch on the body's signed header list. The signature is cryptographically valid at send time but structurally wrong: it covers an ephemeral transport header that is stripped in transit. Fix: sign before injecting the source header, or exclude X-Stoa-Injection-Source from the signed headers list.
